title: Week 33 Quiz — Decolonization and Human Rights

questions.prompt: Which term best matches this definition: The ending of colonial rule and creation or recovery of political sovereignty.
questions.explanation: Decolonization is the course term defined as: The ending of colonial rule and creation or recovery of political sovereignty.

questions.prompt: Which term best matches this definition: The division of territory into separate political units.
questions.explanation: Partition is the course term defined as: The division of territory into separate political units.

questions.prompt: Which term best matches this definition: Organized resistance that rejects physical violence while using protest, boycott, noncooperation, or civil disobedience.
questions.explanation: Nonviolence is the course term defined as: Organized resistance that rejects physical violence while using protest, boycott, noncooperation, or civil disobedience.

questions.prompt: Which term best matches this definition: South Africa’s legally enforced system of racial classification and domination.
questions.explanation: Apartheid is the course term defined as: South Africa’s legally enforced system of racial classification and domination.

questions.prompt: Which term best matches this definition: The 1948 United Nations statement of common human rights principles.
questions.explanation: Universal Declaration Of Human Rights is the course term defined as: The 1948 United Nations statement of common human rights principles.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best accounts for the wave of decolonization after World War II?
choices: One speech caused empires to collapse.
Organized anticolonial movements, imperial weakness, global war, international pressure, and changing ideas of legitimacy interacted differently across cases.
European governments voluntarily ended empire for the same reason everywhere.
Decolonization was entirely a Cold War project.
questions.explanation: Decolonization was multicausal and varied by region; no single factor explains every independence movement.

questions.prompt: India, Ghana, Algeria, and Kenya pursued different paths toward independence. What does that comparison show?
choices: Only armed struggle can produce independence.
Strategies ranged from negotiation and mass nonviolence to armed struggle and international diplomacy, depending on context.
Political organization mattered less than geography.
questions.explanation: Comparative analysis reveals multiple strategies and conditions rather than a universal path to independence.

questions.prompt: A new state inherits colonial borders, export dependence, and administrative institutions. Which claim best avoids colonial determinism?
choices: Colonial rule completely predetermined every later outcome.
Inherited institutions cannot influence later politics.
Colonial legacies constrained choices, but leaders and societies still made consequential post-independence decisions.
questions.explanation: Historical constraints shape possibilities without eliminating later agency or contingency.

questions.prompt: Why compare independence speeches with articles of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights?
choices: To identify shared claims about dignity and self-determination while examining distinct goals, audiences, and strategies.
To prove every independence leader interpreted rights identically.
To replace local evidence with a global document.
To determine which speech is longest.
questions.explanation: The comparison can reveal shared principles and meaningful differences without flattening distinct movements.

questions.prompt: Two countries gain independence with similar income levels but later differ in health, education, inequality, and political rights. What is the strongest conclusion?
choices: Income alone measures the success of independence.
Post-independence development is multidimensional, so several indicators and historical contexts are needed.
The country with higher income automatically has stronger rights.
Later outcomes prove colonial history had no effect.
questions.explanation: Development cannot responsibly be reduced to one indicator; multiple measures reveal different outcomes and tradeoffs.

shortResponse.prompt: Using at least two specific pieces of evidence, answer: How did colonized peoples transform self-determination from a promise into political movements and new states?
shortResponse.exemplar: A full-credit response states a defensible answer to the essential question, uses two accurate details from the week, explains how each detail supports the claim, and acknowledges one complexity or limitation.
